title: Do Multi-Agents Dream of Electric Screens? Achieving 100% on AndroidWorld Through Task Decomposition
abstract: arXiv:2602.07787v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We present Minitap's mobile-use, a multi-agent system for Android UI control, and evaluate it on the 116 tasks of AndroidWorld, on Android emulators in Minitap's cloud device infrastructure, real Pixel 7 phones from our device farm and the stock emulator. On fresh, held-out task instances (three pre-registered seeds never used during development), the final system reaches a pass@3 of 100.0% (95% CI 96.8-100.0); pass^3 is 94.0% (95% CI 89.7-97.4) and the mean success rate 98.0% (95% CI 96.0-99.7). Minitap decomposes each task across five LLM agents (planning, subgoal tracking, state capture, decision, execution) and deterministic nodes, with mechanisms that read typed text back from the device, verify the goal on device evidence and detect repeated failures. A study of the initial system measures what each part contributes: removing only the decomposition changes success by -26.1 [-35.6, -16.7] points, the mechanisms together add +11.

translated_title: 多智能体会梦见电子屏幕吗？通过任务分解在AndroidWorld上实现100%成功率
translated_abstract: 我们提出了Minitap的mobile-use，一个用于Android UI控制的多智能体系统，并在AndroidWorld的116个任务上对其进行评估，评估环境包括Minitap云设备基础设施中的Android模拟器、我们设备农场中的真实Pixel 7手机以及原生模拟器。在全新的、从未在开发中使用的保留任务实例上（三个预注册种子），最终系统达到了100.0%的pass@3（95%置信区间96.8-100.0）；pass^3为94.0%（95%置信区间89.7-97.4），平均成功率为98.0%（95%置信区间96.0-99.7）。Minitap将每个任务分解到五个LLM智能体（规划、子目标跟踪、状态捕获、决策、执行）和确定性节点上，并配备了从设备读回输入文本、基于设备证据验证目标以及检测重复失败等机制。对初始系统的消融研究衡量了各组成部分的贡献：仅移除任务分解就会使成功率下降26.1 [-35.6, -16.7]个百分点，而这些机制合计带来+11个百分点的提升。
tldr: 该论文提出Minitap的mobile-use多智能体系统，通过将任务分解到五个LLM智能体（规划、子目标跟踪、状态捕获、决策、执行）和确定性节点，并辅以设备端文本回读、目标验证与重复失败检测等机制，在AndroidWorld基准的116个任务上实现了100%的pass@3成功率。
en_tdlr: The paper presents Minitap's mobile-use, a multi-agent system that achieves 100% pass@3 on AndroidWorld's 116 tasks by decomposing each task across five LLM agents (planning, subgoal tracking, state capture, decision, execution) plus deterministic nodes, with mechanisms for reading typed text back from the device, verifying goals on device evidence, and detecting repeated failures.
